s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic ankle pain and swelling with bony lesion
salient_findings: Pain and swelling around the right ankle for 1 year
Bony thickening over the lateral malleolus
Submetaphyseal lytic lesion in the distal tibia with a well-defined sclerotic margin
key_facts: 13-year-old boy
1-year history of pain and swelling around the right ankle
Gradually increasing in size
Bony thickening over the lateral malleolus
Ankle and subtalar joints have a full range of motion
Complete blood count within normal limits
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 68 mm at the first hour
Submetaphyseal lytic lesion in the distal tibia with a well-defined sclerotic margin

shortlist.label: Brodie's abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Submetaphyseal lytic lesion with sclerotic margin and elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate

shortlist.label: Osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic pain and swelling with elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate

shortlist.label: Osteoid osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: Bony thickening and pain with well-defined sclerotic margin

shortlist.label: Chondroblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lytic lesion in the distal tibia with sclerotic margin

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Lytic lesion with well-defined sclerotic margin and potential for bone expansion

raw.rationale: The presence of a submetaphyseal lytic lesion in the distal tibia with a well-defined sclerotic margin, along with a significantly elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, is consistent with the diagnosis of Brodie's abscess, a type of chronic osteomyelitis.

rejected.label: Osteomyelitis
rejected.why: While osteomyelitis is related to Brodie's abscess, the specific description of a submetaphyseal lytic lesion with a sclerotic margin more precisely matches Brodie's abscess.

rejected.label: Osteoid osteoma
rejected.why: Osteoid osteoma typically presents with a smaller, more painful lesion, often with a central nidus, which does not match the described large, gradually increasing lesion.

rejected.label: Chondroblastoma
rejected.why: Chondroblastoma is a rare bone tumor that usually occurs in the epiphyses of long bones, which does not align with the submetaphyseal location described.

rejected.label: Giant cell tumor
rejected.why: Giant cell tumor typically occurs in the epiphyseal region of bones and is more common in adults, which does not fit the patient's age and the lesion's location.
